title: Explain the behavioral patterns Observer, Command, Iterator, State, Template Method, Visitor, Mediator, and Memento.
shortTitle: Explain the behavioral patterns Observer, Command, Iterator, State, Template Method, Visitor, Mediator, and Memento
topicTitle: Behavioral: Strategy, Observer, Command, State, Template
keyPoints: Observer notifies many subscribers when a subject changes, decoupling the event source from reactions.
Command packages an action as an object with execute and undo, enabling queuing, logging, and reversal.
Iterator provides sequential access to a collection without exposing its internal structure.
State lets an object change behaviour when its internal state changes, replacing sprawling conditionals with state classes.
Template Method defines an algorithm skeleton in a base method and lets subclasses fill the varying steps.
Visitor adds new operations to a stable set of element classes without modifying them.
In modern Java, Command is often a `Runnable`, Observer listeners are lambdas, and Iterator is hidden inside streams.

s1_definition.oneliner: Observer notifies, Command packages actions, Iterator walks collections, State switches behaviour, Template Method fixes a skeleton, Visitor adds operations, Mediator centralises talk, and Memento snapshots state.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Observer** – defines a one-to-many dependency so when a subject changes, all registered observers are notified automatically.
- **Command** – packages an action as an object with `execute()` and `undo()`, enabling queuing, logging, and reversal.
- **Iterator** – exposes elements of a collection sequentially without revealing its internals.
- **State** – lets an object change behaviour when its internal state changes, as if it changed class.
- **Template Method** – defines the skeleton of an algorithm in a base method and lets subclasses fill specific steps.
- **Visitor** – adds new operations to a stable set of element classes without modifying them.
- **Mediator** – centralises complex communication between objects so they do not reference each other directly.
- **Memento** – captures and restores an object's state without exposing its internals.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India: Observer is the alert system that tells audit, SMS, and the dashboard when a transfer completes. Command is writing each banking instruction on a slip that can be queued, logged, and reversed. Iterator is flipping through a passbook one entry at a time. State is an account behaving differently when ACTIVE versus FROZEN. Template Method is the fixed settlement procedure where only one step changes per instrument. Visitor is the auditor who visits every account and performs a new check without changing the accounts. Mediator is the dealing desk that coordinates traders. Memento is a saved snapshot of an account you can roll back to.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Eight Behavioral Patterns
  ─────────────────────────
  Observer:   Subject ──notify──→ [Observer A, Observer B, Observer C]
  Command:    Invoker ──execute──→ Command ──→ Receiver
  Iterator:   Client ──next()──→ Iterator ──→ Collection
  State:      Context ──delegate──→ [Active | Frozen | Closed]
  Template:   Base.settle() { validate(); execute(); record(); }
                                     ↑ subclass fills this step
  Visitor:    Element.accept(visitor) ──→ visitor.visit(element)
  Mediator:   Trader A ──→ Desk ──→ Trader B, Trader C
  Memento:    Account ──save()──→ Memento ──restore()──→ Account
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Behavioral patterns describe how objects communicate and divide responsibility. Observer defines a one-to-many relationship where a subject notifies all its subscribers on a change, which is how a completed transfer triggers audit, SMS, and dashboard reactions. Command packages an action as an object with execute and undo, so operations can be queued, logged, replayed, or reversed. Iterator gives sequential access to a collection without exposing its internals. State lets an object change behaviour when its internal state changes, replacing sprawling conditionals with clean state classes.

Template Method defines the fixed skeleton of an algorithm and lets subclasses fill the varying steps, which is how a settlement always validates, executes, and records while only the execute step changes per instrument. Visitor adds operations to stable element classes without modifying them. Mediator centralises many-to-many communication so objects do not reference each other directly. And Memento captures and restores an object's state for undo and checkpoints.

In the transaction engine at National Bank of India, these appear together: Rajesh publishes a transfer event to many observers, models debit and credit as reversible commands, uses State so a frozen account rejects withdrawals, and uses a settlement template so the procedure shape is fixed while the instrument-specific step varies.

The senior point is that in modern Java several of these shrink to lambdas: a Command is often just a `Runnable`, Observer listeners are lambdas, and Iterator is hidden inside streams. The pattern intent still guides the design even when the actual Java form is a single line, and recognising both the intent and the lightweight form is what shows real production understanding.

Remember one sentence: behavioral patterns govern how objects communicate, and the eight classics cover notification, action packaging, traversal, state-driven behaviour, algorithm skeletons, operation extension, coordination, and state snapshots.
